candidates.explanation: The duplicate-email check is inverted. It throws emailExists only when the user found by the new email has the same id as the current user. That case can't occur, because the email differs from the current one. When the email belongs to a different account, no error is thrown. The confirmation hash is signed and the mail is sent, and the request returns 200. The condition should be `userByEmail && userByEmail.id !== currentUser.id`, or simply `if (userByEmail)`.

fix.description: In AuthService.update, change the condition `userByEmail && userByEmail.id === currentUser.id` to `userByEmail && userByEmail.id !== currentUser.id`. Because the new email already differs from the current one, plain `if (userByEmail)` also works. Optionally re-check uniqueness in confirmNewEmail, since the email could be taken between the request and the confirmation.

candidates.explanation: The duplicate-email check is inverted. It throws emailExists only when the user found by the new email has the same id as the current user. That case can't occur, because the email differs from the current one. When the email belongs to a different account, no error is thrown. The confirmation hash is signed and the mail is sent, and the request returns 200. The condition should be `userByEmail && userByEmail.id !== currentUser.id`, or simply `if (userByEmail)`.

fix.description: In AuthService.update, change the condition `userByEmail && userByEmail.id === currentUser.id` to `userByEmail && userByEmail.id !== currentUser.id`. Because the new email already differs from the current one, plain `if (userByEmail)` also works. Optionally re-check uniqueness in confirmNewEmail, since the email could be taken between the request and the confirmation.
